title: CRLR/157/2010 of AADESH JAIN ALIAS UBHAI JAIN Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 157 of 2010
Aadesh Jain @ Ubhai Jain ....... Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand .......Respondent
Present:
Mr. Shashi Kant Shandilya, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, Deputy Advocate General for the State.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.(Oral)
Revisionist Aadesh Jain @ Ubhai Jain preferred an
instant revision, challenging the following judgment and orders:-
(i) Judgment and order dated 28.02.2008 passed in
Criminal Case No. 293 of 2007, State Vs. Aadesh
Jain @ Ubhai Jain and connected matters (for
short "the case"), by which, the revisionist has
been sentenced under Section 25 of the Arms Act,
1959 (for short "the Act") and sentenced to one
year's simple imprisonment with a fine of
Rs.500/-. In default of payment of fine to undergo
simple imprisonment for further period of one
month.
(ii) Judgment and order dated 19.05.2010, passed in
Criminal Appeal No. 7 of 2008, Aadesh @ Ubhai
Jain Vs. State, by the Court of learned District and
Sessions Judge, Roorkee, District Haridwar (for
short "the appeal") by which, judgment and order
dated 28.02.2008, passed in the case has been
confirmed.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties through video
conferencing and perused the records.

2
3. Facts necessary for disposal of this revision, briefly
stated, are that on 14.04.2007, according to the prosecution, at about
4:15 PM, the revisionist alongwith other persons were intercepted by
the Police. From the possession of the revisionist, a country-made
pistol, 315 bore alongwith one cartridge were recovered. Based on
this recovery, Case Crime No. 82 of 2007 was registered against the
revisionist. The matter was investigated, in which, after investigation,
charge sheet under Section 25 of the Act was submitted. On
13.06.2007, charge under Section 25 of the Act was framed against
the revisionist, to which, he denied and claimed trial.
4. In order to prove the case, prosecution examined three
witnesses, namely, PW1 Sarvesh Kumar Aggarwal, the person, who
recovered the firearms from the possession of the revisionist, PW2
Constable, Amit Kumar, who accompanied PW1 Sarvesh Kumar
Aggarwal, when the recovery was made and PW3 K.C. Bhatt, who
investigated the matter. The revisionist was examined under Section
313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and by an impugned
judgment and order passed in the case, the revisionist has been
convicted and sentenced as stated hereinbefore. Against which, an
appeal was preferred, which, as stated, has also been dismissed.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist would raise one
argument alone that is non compliance of Section 39 of the Act.
According to learned counsel, in the instant case, the sanction for
prosecution has not been proved and it vitiates the conviction.
According to him, in fact, the charge sheet was prepared on
11.04.2007, whereas, the document purportedly for prosecution
sanction was obtained on 13.05.2007.
6. On behalf of the State, it is argued that charge sheet was
filed in the court on 01.06.2007, therefore, according to learned State
counsel the revisionist is not entitled to get benefit of the fact that
sanction for prosecution was accorded on 30.05.2007.

3
7. This Court requested, learned State counsel to tell as to
where is the legally admissible evidence with regard to the sanction
for prosecution under Section 39 of the Act. To it, learned State
counsel would reply that sanction for prosecution has not been
proved.
8. Sanction for prosecution is provided under Section 39 of
the Act, which reads as hereunder:-
"Previous sanction of the district magistrate necessary
in certain cases.-No prosecution shall be instituted against any
person in respect of any offence under section 3 without the
previous sanction of the district magistrate."
9. Needless to say, the act of according sanction for
prosecution is not a formal act, it requires that the District Magistrate
would judiciously consider the matter for grant or refusal of the
sanction under the Act.
10. In the instant case, the same argument was advanced at
the trial, but learned court below observed that since charge sheet was
filed on 01.06.2007 and prosecution sanction was accorded on
30.05.2007, it does not make any difference.
11. PW1 Sarvesh Kumar Aggarwal and PW2 Amit Kumar
have proved the recovery memo Ex. A1. PW3 K.C.Bhatt is an
Investigating Officer, who proved some other documents prepared
during investigation, including site plan of the place of recovery and
charge sheet in the instant case, which is Ex A3. He also proves the
General Diary entries. But, Investigating Officer also did not tell even
a single word about the prosecution sanction. None of the witnesses
have stated about prosecution sanction.
12. The Investigating Officer, PW3 K.C. Bhatt proves
charge sheet Ex. A3, which he signed on 11.04.2007. It means,
whatever was to be done by Investigating Officer, he had done on

4
11.04.2007. Thereafter, the charge sheet might have been routed
through some official channels for its submission before the court.
13. The question is as to when was the prosecution sanction
accorded? There is a document on record of the case, which is
marked at Paper No. 6A, signed by some District Magistrate on
30.05.2007. But, who obtained this sanction? How the District
Magistrate on 30.05.2007 perused the firearms? Who took the
firearms from police Maalkhana and placed it before the District
Magistrate? Who took the firearms back to the Maalkhana? Where is
that Maalkhana entry? Where is the evidence to establish that the
allegedly recovered articles were safely kept in police custody and
safely placed before the District Magistrate and safely returned to the
police Maalkhana? There is no evidence at all, what to say on chain
of evidence.
14. The document relating to sanction has not been proved.
Is it really signed by the District Magistrate? There is no evidence to
this fact. Prosecution utterly failed to prove that any sanction was
accorded in the instant case. In the instant case, legally no sanction
was accorded to prosecute the revisionist and it alone vitiates the
conviction, therefore, the revision deserves to be allowed.
15. The revision is allowed. Both the impugned judgment
and orders are set aside. Revisionist is acquitted of the charge under
Section 25 of the Act. Revisionist is on bail. He needs not to
surrender.
16. Let a copy of this judgment along with Lower Court
Record be transmitted to the Court below for compliance
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
13.08.2020
Jitendra
